title: FamilyMart Socks Save Uzbekistan at Asian Games
paragraphs: Japanese convenience stores are famous for selling almost everything people might need. At this year's Asian Games in Japan, one of them even came to the rescue of a national sports team.

The 2026 Asian Games were held in Aichi Prefecture and its capital, Nagoya. When Uzbekistan's men's volleyball team arrived in Nagoya before its first match, the players discovered a problem. Team members had packed different kinds of socks. However, the Asian Games' rules on uniforms require all players on a team to wear socks that match in color, length and pattern.

Fortunately, there was a branch of the convenience store chain FamilyMart near the team's hotel. FamilyMart sells its own brand of socks, and the team was able to buy enough matching pairs for all the players. The socks, called "Line Socks," are white with blue and green stripes. These colors match both the Uzbek flag and FamilyMart's own company colors. Each pair costs 429 yen.

The team played its first match against Japan on September 27. Japan won the match in straight sets. However, many people watching on television were also interested in the Uzbek players' socks, and they wondered whether they had come from a convenience store. Later, two of the players confirmed in an interview that they had bought the socks at FamilyMart.
FamilyMart was delighted with the attention. The company said it was happy to have been able to help on such a major sporting stage.

The story may also lead to closer business ties. At a later meeting at the Uzbek Embassy in Tokyo, FamilyMart executive Nana Shimada and Uzbek officials discussed the attention that the athletes had brought to the company. According to reports, FamilyMart is now considering expanding its cooperation with Uzbekistan, including importing more Uzbek textiles and food products into Japan. However, no agreement has been confirmed yet.
For now, the story is a reminder that sometimes the solution to a big problem can be found at the convenience store around the corner.
